findings.reason: the pull should read its COCOS class and sign through `imas_codex/cocos/` rather than store a second, independent notion of "sign to target COCOS", or it must say why that owner cannot supply it.
findings.text: §1 and §3 make the plan's central convention decision ("record `channel_factor` as the total sign to the rule's target COCOS and take the class from the DD, never from the rule's `transformation` field") by re-deriving COCOS sign/class semantics that `imas_codex/cocos/` already owns: `cocos_from_dd_version` (calculator.py:127), `determine_cocos` (158), `validate_cocos_from_data` (345), and `path_needs_cocos_transform` / `get_sign_flip_paths` (transforms.py:30,54), which already read the DD's psi_like labelling; the plan never cites this package

findings.reason: the author must either place the pull under a distinct verb/namespace or justify overloading `map`, because `imas-codex imas map …` currently means the mapping pipeline to every existing user and test.
findings.text: `imas map` already names the source→IMAS mapping pipeline (`run/status/show/validate/clear/activate`, registered at `imas_codex/cli/imas_dd.py:58`), and §3 adds `imas map pull` under the same group for machine-map rules, giving the `map` namespace a second, unrelated meaning; the plan lists `cli/map.py` as a write path but never notes the namespace is taken

findings.reason: the design must either link rules through `MappingEvidence`/`HAS_EVIDENCE` or state why a new evidence carrier is needed, so a later reader does not find two evidence stores for one convention question.
findings.text: §1/§4 treat "a pulled rule is evidence" and hand it to the conventions stage, but the schema already owns evidence: `Evidence` (facility.yaml:1369) and `MappingEvidence` (facility.yaml:3051) with `EvidenceType` (facility.yaml:202), whose `cocos` value is literally "Evidence from COCOS or sign convention analysis"; the plan names none of these

findings.reason: the join should be expressed on the existing `SignalSource` edges (with the plan naming which), or the author must justify a parallel join edge, and the census of SignalSource edges the pull touches should be listed.
findings.text: §3 "joins it to its source and target" without naming the `SignalSource` edges that already own that relationship: `maps_to_imas` (MAPS_TO_IMAS, facility.yaml:2163), `mapping_candidates` (MAPPING_CANDIDATE, :2179) and `has_evidence` (HAS_EVIDENCE → MappingEvidence, :2193); a rule that "joins a SignalSource and an IMASNode" is exactly the join these edges carry

findings.reason: §2's design should cite these facility-local version idioms and decide whether the pulled bundle reuses or deliberately departs from them, so the version/change shape is not settled four times independently.
findings.text: §2 designs "a bundle-version node" plus "a change record on the rule" and cites only the DD/standard-name idioms, but the facility schema owns two versioned-change precedents it never cites: `SignalEpoch` (facility.yaml:1739) already records a structural version with per-version deltas (`nodes_added_from_previous`, `subtrees_added_removed` at :1772-1782) and `SourceVersion` (facility_config.yaml:703) is a version node for a data source

findings.reason: at zero headroom every added interface must be accounted for in the section's own text, so the section must state what surface it retires or merges (e.g. reusing the `map` group rather than a new verb) or why no retirement is possible.
findings.text: §3 adds `imas map pull FACILITY --bundle PATH` (a CLI subcommand plus option) and new node and change-record classes, while the supplied figures are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0, and the section names nothing it retires or merges and states no reason nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the capability lands as one new module (`imas_codex/ids/external_maps.py`) whose shape §2 is the node that settles, and the read-side consumers extend existing owners (`discovery/signals/conventions.py`, `ids/slot_context.py`) rather than each wrapping the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 joins a rule to a source and target without naming the `SignalSource` edges that already own that join, and §1/§4 call a pulled rule "evidence" without naming the `Evidence`/`MappingEvidence` classes that own evidence.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 adds a CLI subcommand and option plus node/edge classes and neither names what it retires or merges nor states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the DD and standard-name change idioms but never searched `imas_codex/cocos/`, the package that already owns COCOS sign/class semantics, nor the existing `imas map` CLI namespace.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §4 extends the conventions module owned by `signal-cocos-conventions` §7 and the existing `ids/slot_context.py` instead of writing a parallel evidence reader, which is the extension the item asks for; no thin wrapper is proposed.
